hints: Focus on the conditions, hot concentrated acidified manganate(VII) means vigorous oxidative cleavage of every C=C bond, not mild diol formation.
Count the double bonds in limonene, there is one trisubstituted C=C inside the ring and one terminal C(CH3)=CH2 group outside the ring.
Recall what each alkene pattern gives on cleavage, =CH2 gives CO2, =C(CH3)- gives CH3CO-, and =CH- gives -CO2H, then see which large fragment fits.
walkthrough:
**Recall the reagent rule**

Hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves the C=C bond completely. Each alkene carbon is oxidised separately.

$$\text{>C=C<} \rightarrow \text{carbonyls / acids + } \text{CO}_2$$

**Cleave the ring double bond**

The top bond is $(\text{CH}_3)\text{C}=\text{CH}-$. The $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)$ end has no H, so it becomes a methyl ketone, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. The $\text{CH}$ end has one H, so under vigorous conditions it becomes a carboxylic acid, $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. This opens the six-membered ring into a chain.

**Cleave the side-chain double bond**

The bottom group is $-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$. The $-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$ end stays attached to the opened chain and becomes $-\text{COCH}_3$. The terminal $=\text{CH}_2$ fragment is oxidised right through to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$$\text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Assemble the products**

Joining the two cleaved ends together gives one large keto-acid-diketone: $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{COCH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. That is compound 3, plus $\text{CO}_2$ which is compound 2. Compound 1 with two $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups is not formed.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all formed. While 2 and 3 are correct, 1 is wrong because the ring C(CH3)= carbon gives a ketone CH3CO-, not an acid, and the side chain C(CH3)= also gives a ketone, so the product must have two ketones and one acid.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 only. Compound 1, CH3COCH2CH2CH(CH2CO2H)2, has one ketone and two acids. That would require two =CH- carbons, but limonene has only one =CH- in the ring. The side chain gives CH3CO-, not CH2CO2H.
options.C: Correct. Vigorous cleavage of the ring (CH3)C=CH- gives CH3CO- and -CO2H, and cleavage of -C(CH3)=CH2 gives -COCH3 attached to the chain plus CO2. The combined organic fragment is CH3COCH2CH2CH(COCH3)CH2CO2H (3) plus CO2 (2).
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only 1. Compound 1 is not produced at all, and it misses the CO2 evolved from the terminal =CH2 group, which is always oxidised to CO2 under hot concentrated conditions.
